references.text: Jacob builds an altar in Shechem and calls it El-Elohe-Israel ('God, the God of Israel'), reflecting his new identity after meeting God at Peniel.
Hosea refers back to Jacob's struggle with the angel at Peniel, where he wept and begged for mercy – a direct reference to the event in Gen 32.
Jacob worshipped God leaning on the top of his staff. Tradition links this to his limping after the struggle at Peniel.
During the struggle at Peniel, Jacob's hip socket was dislocated, which explains why he limped as the sun rose over him.
